text: If you're in your 20s and you're still a virgin, I have a genuine amount of respect for you because that means you possess a lot of self-control. That means you have a great deal of respect for your body, your mind, your soul, and you're waiting for your partner. Guaranteed, if you try to abstain from this stuff as much as you can, then you will be so much happier with your future partner. Versus somebody who has a body count of like 50 or 60, something crazy. Look, I get what this guy is trying to do. He's trying to be nice, supportive, make guys who are still virgins in their 20s feel better about it. It is fine, it is self-control, it is virtue. But you know what they say? The road to hell is paved with good intentions. This kind of message, honestly, can ruin a lot of men. Because what it really teaches is inaction. To sit and wait, to tell yourself, it will be fine, someday the right girl will just appear. Let me tell you something, it won't. The less experience you have with women, the harder it becomes to actually connect. You start overthinking everything, putting women on a pedestal, and when, and if, you finally meet one, you treat her like she is the only thing that exists for you in this world, which eventually backfires. You don't learn confidence by avoiding women. You learn it by living life, talking to the ladies, getting rejected, making mistakes, and realizing that women are just human too. Every guy who hides behind this self-control excuse ends up being 30 or 40 with no clue on how to talk to women. And don't get me wrong, if you truly choose to wait, that is your decision. But don't make it sound like a virtue. Most guys who say, I am waiting, are not waiting out of principle. They are waiting out of fear. Fear of rejection, fear of looking stupid, fear of being inexperienced. So stop lying to yourself. If you want to have a woman in your life, go outside, talk to the ladies, get rejected, learn, improve. You don't need to wait for the right one, you need to become the right one, for yourself first.
